title: Emotion Regulation Therapy as mechanism-targeted intervention for high distress disorders
summary: Patients with depression who have experienced adverse events in childhood often suffer from particularly severe symptoms. These symptoms are usually accompanied with high psychological distress which involves difficulties in effectively managing stress and negative emotions, as well as heightened vigilance toward potential threats. Therefore, this study aims to examine for the first time whether a specialized therapeutic approach (Emotion Regulation Therapy), specifically addressing these difficulties, is feasible. Patients will be randomly assigned either to Emotion Regulation Therapy or to an established cognitive-behavioral therapy. Both treatments consist of 24 sessions, conducted twice weekly. The primary aim is to assess the feasibility of implementing the therapy and to gather initial indications of its potential effectiveness. These findings will serve as a basis for future, more comprehensive studies.
conditions: Depressive Disorders and adverse childhood experiences

interventions.name:
24 sessions of Emotion Regulation Therapy, with self-monitoring, acquisition of attention-based and metacognitive skills for emotion regulation, and development of value-based actions as essential components
(50 minutes each, two sessions per week)

24 sessions of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, with behavioral activation, cognitive therapy and social and problem solving skills training
(50 minutes each, two sessions per week)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of a depressive disorder (F32.x, F33.x) as primary disorder and treatment focus
PHQ-9 score > 9
PTQ score > 35
K10 Distress Scale > 23
Presence of adverse childhood experiences (assessed with ACE-D)
Sufficient proficiency in German
Exclusion criteria:
Outpatient psychotherapy within the past 2 years
Initiation of new antidepressant medication within the 3 months prior to baseline assessment
Dose adjustment of antidepressant medication within 4 weeks prior to baseline assessment
Discontinuation of antidepressant medication within 4 weeks prior to baseline assessment
Acute suicidality
Current substance use disorder (except tobacco)
Bipolar affective disorders
Current post-traumatic stress disorder
Lifetime diagnosis of borderline personality disorder
Current psychotic symptoms
Body Mass Index < 17.5
Severe physical impairments interfering with outpatient psychotherapy
